9	## 1. The ladder
10	
11	The Guidebook's evidence tiers run T1–T6 with two parallel community-knowledge tracks (Co-1, Co-2). Outer ranks are not "higher quality" in a vacuum — they answer different questions. **Tier number reflects what kind of claim a source can anchor, not how good the source is.**
12	
13	| Tier | Evidence character | Typical `evidence_type` | What it can anchor |
14	|---|---|---|---|
15	| **T1** | Primary research with intervention-level or biomechanical control on the parameter under design | `clinical`, occasionally `grey` for unpublished primary | Best-practice claims that turn on physiological / behavioural / biomechanical mechanism |
16	| **Co-1** | Disability-led lived-experience publications — DPOs, named-org Deaf / blind / wheelchair-user / mental-health / autism-organisation outputs; CRPD Art. 4.3 consultation outputs | `co1` | Best-practice claims that turn on user-stated preference, dignity, autonomy, or self-determined accommodation. Co-1 ranks alongside T1 because primary-research evidence and lived-experience evidence are non-substitutable on different claim types |
17	| **T2** | Community-consensus synthesis above primary studies but below international standards. Two streams: (a) systematic reviews / meta-analyses; (b) named-organisation evidence-based standards (DPO guidelines, professional-body standards) | `sr_meta`, `standard_eb`, occasionally `co2` for community-of-professional synthesis | Best-practice claims that turn on synthesised evidence across multiple primary studies, OR on professional-body / DPO position |
18	| **Co-2** | OT / professional-body CPGs (CAOT, AOTA, RCOT, COTEC, WFOT, national equivalents) | `co2` | Best-practice claims that turn on clinical-professional consensus on rehabilitation or activity-of-daily-living adaptation |
19	| **T3** | Clinical primary research at lower control level (cross-sectional, observational, qualitative, single-centre) plus grey-literature primary research | `clinical` (predominant), `grey`, occasionally `standard_eb` for specialised technical guidance | Supporting evidence for best-practice claims; rarely the sole basis |
20	| **T4** | International standards (ISO, IEC, CEN, BSI PAS, EN 81-70, EN 17210, etc.) — published by international bodies; legally significant within their adoption scope | `standard_eb` (predominant) | Code-baseline citations of international harmonisation; supporting evidence for best-practice claims if the standard itself rests on T1/T2 evidence |
21	| **T5** | National beyond-code frameworks — best-practice guidance issued by national bodies but not legally enforced (BS 8300, DIN 18040 draft, Boverket BBR advisories, national CPGs scoped to BE) | `national_fw` (predominant), `standard_eb` | Code-baseline citations at national best-practice tier; supporting evidence for best-practice claims if the framework rests on T1/T2 evidence |
22	| **T6** | Statutory code — legally enforceable national / sub-national accessibility code (ADA, AS 1428.1, NZS 4121, EN 81-70 when adopted as legal compliance, NZ Building Code D1/AS1, Approved Document M Vol 2, AS/NZS, GB 50763, MLIT barrier-free law, etc.) | `code` | **Code-baseline citations.** Tier 6 establishes regulatory floor. ⚠ Superseded by §8 + Option A (2026-07-21): T6 anchors a **weak-band (○) "best practice as currently known"** claim, flagged code-derived; the convergence of multiple T6 codes on a value is convergence-not-evidence (see §3), retained as the weak-band honesty rule |

24	## 2. sr_meta placement — T2, not T3
25	
26	The decision: systematic reviews and meta-analyses sit at **Tier 2** alongside named-organisation evidence-based standards.
27	
28	The reasoning, in declining priority:
29	
30	1. **PI v10.14 line 138 reading.** Rule #9 step 5 enumerates "Tier 1 / Co-1 / Tier 2 / Co-2 / Tier 3 evidence" with T4 / T5 explicitly excluded ("Tier 4 international / Tier 5 national-recommended excluded at this step"). The natural reading positions T2 as the synthesis-tier above T3 primary clinical work and below international standards. SR / meta-analysis is the canonical example of synthesis above primary studies.
31	2. **Evidence-type homology.** T2's other occupants (`standard_eb` from named DPOs / professional bodies) are themselves synthesis-tier — they aggregate primary evidence into a consensus position. SR / meta-analysis aggregates primary evidence into a statistical consensus position. Same epistemic move, different machinery.
32	3. **Citation behaviour.** When a Guidebook claim cites both an SR and a primary clinical study, the SR is treated as the warrant-source and the primary study as one of the inputs the SR weighed. The warrant-source must rank above the input-source. SR > primary clinical.
33	4. **GRADE alignment.** The GRADE framework places systematic reviews / meta-analyses of RCTs at the top of the evidence-quality hierarchy. The Guidebook does not adopt GRADE wholesale (the Guidebook reads built-environment claims rather than treatment-effect claims), but the synthesis-above-primary principle is the same.
34	
35	The four sr_meta rows previously sitting at T3 are migrated to T2 by `scripts/migrations/data_20260525070000_sr_meta_t2_canonicalization.sql`.
36	
37	**Scoping reviews and conceptual/framework papers are T3, not T2 (DR-2026-07-21).** `sr_meta` (T2) is reserved for *systematic* reviews and meta-analyses — a defined method with risk-of-bias appraisal and/or effect synthesis. A **scoping review** maps a literature without appraisal (a weaker synthesis) and anchors at **T3**; a peer-reviewed **conceptual/framework paper** (e.g. a design-index proposal such as ASPECTSS) is primary work, also **T3**. Relatedly (DR-2026-07-21): **national accessibility standards** (DIN 18040, BS 8300) and **professional-body design guides** (e.g. the RIBA/Habinteg Inclusive Housing Design Guide) sit at **T5** `national_fw` at the standard/guidance level — a specific provision only becomes T6 when cited as a legally-enforceable adopted code floor (the T5-vs-T6 split already drawn in §1's table).

39	## 3. Best-practice ≠ convergence
40	
41	A separate canonical clarification, surfaced 2026-05-25 during reverification scoping.
42	
43	**The convergence-not-evidence trap.** A claim of the form "BS 8300, DIN 18040-1, Part M, and AS 1428.1 all specify X" is a **convergence claim across Tier 4–6 sources**. Convergence is informative — it tells us multiple jurisdictions adopted the same value. Convergence is NOT best-practice evidence — the jurisdictions could all be wrong together, or could all be reading from a single shared earlier source that itself rests on no evidence, or could all reflect pre-evidence regulatory floors that no jurisdiction has updated.
44	
45	**The corridor-width worked example.** Multiple Tier 5/6 codes converge on 1800mm two-wheelchair-passing. Co-1/T2/T3 evidence (DSDG Bauman 2010, DeafScape Vaughn 2018, Cloete & Rout 2025) anchors 2440mm primary corridors. The 1800mm convergence describes the regulatory floor; the 2440mm Co-1/T2/T3 anchor describes best practice. Labelling 1800mm "preferred" or "best practice" because it converges across T5/T6 jurisdictions is the failure mode this section names.
46	
47	**The implication for citation tiering.** Tier 4–6 citations are valid for code-baseline claims (this is the legal floor in jurisdiction X) and for jurisdiction-tracking work.
48	
49	> **⚠ Superseded 2026-07-20 by §8.** The original text here read *"they do not — by themselves — anchor best-practice claims. Best-practice claims require T1, Co-1, T2, or Co-2 evidence."* That binary is replaced by the **weighted-strength anchor model** (§8): a T4–T6-only claim *may* be stated, but is rendered at partial/weak strength with an explicit honesty flag. The convergence-not-evidence principle above is retained as the honesty rule for the weak band.

51	## 4. Code-currency check is part of citing T4–T6
52	
53	When a BPC cites a T4–T6 source, the citation must additionally confirm that the cited edition is the **current legally-in-force edition** — not a superseded edition. Pre-existing supersession_check rows surface this for the supersession protocol; the same check applies inline to any new T4–T6 citation.
54	
55	**Enforcement.** The currency fact is carried in the `evidence_sources.code_currency_*` columns; no mechanical check reads it since `scripts/audit/code_currency_audit.py` was deleted (plan step 1.6, RULINGS R4).
56	
57	`code_currency_status` enum: `VERIFIED-CURRENT`, `PERMANENT-FRAMEWORK` (foundational references like CRPD, ICF, WHO Child Growth Standards that do not revise on the same cadence), `SUPERSEDED-PENDING-REPLACEMENT`, `UNVERIFIED-CHECK-DEFERRED` (e.g., T6 codes flagged in MOB Pass-2 supersession audit as out-of-scope per DR-2026-05-24).
58	
59	Worked example surfaced 2026-05-25: `accessible-circulation-geometry.md` cites DIN 18040-1:2010-10. The 2010 edition is still legally in force in Germany (referenced in MVV TB 2024/1 published August 2024), but draft revision E DIN 18040-1:2023-02 exists and DIN EN 17210:2021 has been published as the European harmonised accessibility standard. A reverification of the BPC must consider whether the 2010 citation should be retained, supplemented, or replaced. Counter-example same day: NZS 4121:2001 is 24 years old but remains the NZ Building Act §119 / D1/AS1 Acceptable Solution per NZ Ministry of Education March 2025 guidance; age does NOT predict supersession.

61	## 5. evidence_quality marker mapping
62	
63	`skills/guidebook-auditor_SKILL.md` §4.2 inline quality markers map to the canonical ladder:
64	- `●` confirmed evidence base: T1, T2 (sr_meta + standard_eb + co2), **T3 clinical** (lower-control primary clinical research — confirmed primary evidence, lower control level), Co-1, Co-2
65	- `◐` policy or standards basis only, not primary evidence: T4, T5
66	- `○` grey literature, expert consensus, thin base, unconfirmed: T3 grey, `[EXPERT CONSENSUS]`, `[THIN BASE]`, `[UNSUPPORTED]`, T6 (code-floor), a source that could not be retrieved and so stays `UNVERIFIED` (owner, 2026-10-21: it cannot be claimed as primary evidence or at a top tier)
67	
68	The T3 split is deliberate: T3 holds two species (per §1) — lower-control *primary clinical* research and *grey-literature* primary research. The clinical species is confirmed primary evidence (just lower control) and maps to `●`; the grey species maps to `○`. The earlier version of this map listed only "T3 grey → ○" and left T3-clinical unplaced (R9-c).
69	
70	## 6. Mapping back to legacy guidebook-auditor SKILL §4.1
71	
72	The previous guidebook-auditor SKILL §4.1 had `[Tier 4]` = systematic review / meta-analysis. That mapping is **superseded**. SR / meta-analysis is `[Tier 2]` per this document. The SKILL file is amended in lock-step with this canonicalization.
73	
74	## 7. Migration provenance
75	
76	| Element | Source |
77	|---|---|
78	| Owner decision | 2026-05-25 directive "t2>t3 this is enshrined" |
79	| Migration | `scripts/migrations/data_20260525070000_sr_meta_t2_canonicalization.sql` |
80	| Gap closure | GAP-273 (CLOSED-FIXED), GAP-296 (CLOSED-FIXED) |
81	| Skill amendment | `skills/guidebook-auditor_SKILL.md` §4.1 |
82	| Session | `session_2026-05-23-bpc-rewrite-phase-b-closure` |
83	
84	## 8. Weighted-strength anchor model (2026-07-20)
85	
86	Enshrined by `decisions/DR-2026-07-20-weighted-strength-anchor-model.md` per owner directive. **Supersedes the binary rule in §3** ("best-practice claims require T1/Co-1/T2/Co-2").
87	
88	**Every tier can anchor a best-practice claim; the strength of the claim is weighted by the tier of its evidence.** The tiers exist so a reader can grade the confidence behind each proposal — not to gate whether a proposal may be stated. Three strength bands (the `●◐○` markers of §5, now with anchoring semantics):
89	
90	| Band | Tiers | Anchoring behaviour |
91	|---|---|---|
92	| **● Full** | T1, Co-1, T2, Co-2, T3-clinical | Full strength (adjudicated evidence). |
93	| **◐ Partial** | T4, T5 | Anchors, rendered as *current standards practice* — flagged "standards basis, not primary evidence." |
94	| **○ Weak** | T3-grey, T6 (code-floor), expert-consensus / thin base, an unretrievable (`UNVERIFIED`) source | Anchors only a floor/convergence claim, rendered with the flag: *"best available given current regulation/practice, NOT academically adjudicated."* An unretrievable source keeps its tier and may still anchor a determination (D-0157: a return pass is owed), but it earns no band above ○ and is flagged unverified (`has_unverified_sources`) in place of that flag. |
95	
96	A band grades the strength of a claim; it does not set the cell's state (`governance/evidence-methodology.md` §2.2): T3-clinical alone is full band and `provisional`; T3-grey alone is weak band and `pending`.
97	
98	Convergence-not-evidence (§3) is retained as the honesty rule within the weak band. **Amended 2026-07-21 (owner directive, Option A; `decisions/DR-2026-07-21-evidence-architecture-option-a-execution.md`):** a T4–T6-only determination *is* rendered as **weak-band (○) "best practice as currently known"** — best available given that nothing stronger says otherwise — always flagged weak/code-derived with the convergence-not-evidence caveat, never unflagged and never above the ○ band. This supersedes the prior wording ("never relabelled 'best practice'"): such a claim is now stated-and-flagged as weak-band best practice, not suppressed and not merely labelled "regulatory floor," when no stronger evidence exists. **Band assignment at determination level:** a cell whose entire basis is T4–T6 takes ○ even where T4/T5 sources are present; the ◐ "current standards practice" band in the table above applies to individual T4/T5 *citations* within an otherwise-anchored cell, and to source-level `●◐○` markers (§5), which are unchanged (DR-2026-07-21 §2.3).
99	
100	## 9. Review-species tiering (closes GAP-298)
101	
102	- **Systematic reviews / meta-analyses → T2** (`sr_meta`) — unchanged (§2).
103	- **Scoping reviews and narrative / literature reviews → T3** (`clinical`/`grey`, never `sr_meta`): they map breadth without graded critical-appraisal synthesis, so they are *supporting* (● band) but not a T2 synthesis anchor.
104	- **Rapid reviews → case-by-case:** T2 only if a systematic search + appraisal was retained; else T3 (default).
105	
106	## 10. Practitioner / firm practice-stream (closes GAP-299)
107	
108	Practitioner and firm design work (architects, accessibility consultants) is placed **by method, not authorship**, and sits **below Co-1 and Co-2 in authority**:
109	- Firm POE / measured study (outcome or cost data) → primary evidence at its method tier (T1/T3).
110	- Firm framework/index that genuinely synthesises evidence → T2-adjacent; else supporting (T3).
111	- Firm guidance/white-paper without method → T3-grey (○ weak).
112	
113	**Role-appropriate-authority gate.** A firm/architect source can anchor a *descriptive/measured* claim (what was built, cost, measured) at its method strength, but **cannot anchor a functional-need claim** ("disabled people need X / X works because Y") on its own — that requires **Co-1** (lived experience) or **Co-2** (OT). A firm asserting a functional-need claim alone is flagged *"designer assertion, unadjudicated."* A dedicated `practice` (Co-3) encoding is defined in the DR; its audit representation is deferred to the audit rework.

412	def gather_extraction_links(conn, parameter_id, governing_refs):
413	    """Every extraction for this parameter, graded by the part it played.
414	
415	    THE BACKWARD WALK STARTS HERE (migration 077). `gather_sources` returns SOURCES and
416	    its DISTINCT is load-bearing -- collapsing the 1:N fan-out is what stops one document
417	    corroborating itself -- so it cannot also tell us WHICH rows governed. This does, and
418	    the two are deliberately separate functions rather than one that returns both: the
419	    first answers "how many independent sources", the second "which sentences", and
420	    conflating them is how the fan-out collapse would leak into the provenance record.
421	
422	    Returns one dict per extraction, with `role` in:
423	
424	      governing     figure_role supplies a value AND the row's source survived the tier,
425	                    verification and supersession gates -- i.e. its ref_id is in the
426	                    governing set this determination actually used.
427	      conditioning  figure_role='condition'. Qualifies a governing row. Carried onto the
428	                    determination so a slope arrives with its run length attached.
429	      excluded      everything else, with a MANDATORY reason. This is the row that makes
430	                    a `pending` cell legible: "examined, and here is why it did not
431	                    answer" reads differently from silence, and the two were previously
432	                    indistinguishable to everything except a hash collision.
433	
434	    Two facts ride along on each dict, beside the role, for the caller to report: `superseded`
435	    (the row's source has been replaced, so it is not gathered) and, on a `finding` row only,
436	    `left_out`: "skimmed" or "absent" when the row supplies no direction (`gather_findings`) and
437	    its source is still current. A skimmed one owes a dedicated reading.
438	
439	    `governing_refs` is passed in rather than re-derived because the caller has already
440	    applied the tier/verification/supersession gates; re-deriving them here would be a
441	    second implementation of the anchoring rule, free to drift from the first.
442	    """
443	    # Positional, not by name: this module's connection carries no row_factory, and
444	    # assuming one made the first cut of this function raise `tuple indices must be
445	    # integers`. The column order here is the SELECT's, which is the only contract.
446	    method_col = ("x.extraction_method"
447	                  if _has_column(conn, "source_value_extractions", "extraction_method")
448	                  else "NULL")
449	    rows = conn.execute(
450	        f"SELECT x.extraction_id, x.ref_id, x.figure_role, x.claim_type, {method_col}, "
451	        "e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NOT NULL FROM source_value_extractions x "
452	        "LEFT JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = x.ref_id "
453	        "WHERE x.parameter_id = ? ORDER BY x.extraction_id", (parameter_id,)).fetchall()
454	    gov = set(governing_refs or ())
455	    out = []
456	    for eid, ref, frole, ctype, method, superseded in rows:
457	        left_out = None
458	        if frole in VALUE_SUPPLYING_ROLES and method in NOT_PUBLISHABLE_METHODS:
459	            # Checked BEFORE the governing branch: a skimmed row is left out even when its
460	            # source governs through another, fully read row (owner 2026-10-09).
461	            role, why = "excluded", (
462	                f"extraction_method={method!r}: a skimmed figure is not publishable "
463	                f"(owner ruling 2026-10-09, 'skimmed values are not publishable'); it is "
464	                f"recorded and shown, never set as the value")
465	        elif frole in VALUE_SUPPLYING_ROLES and ref in gov:
466	            role, why = "governing", None
467	        elif frole in CONDITIONING_ROLES:
468	            role, why = "conditioning", None
469	        elif frole in VALUE_SUPPLYING_ROLES:
470	            # Value-supplying, but its source did not survive the anchoring gates.
471	            role, why = "excluded", (
472	                f"figure_role={frole!r} supplies a value, but {ref} is not in the "
473	                f"governing set: it was disqualified on tier, verification or "
474	                f"supersession before the value was reached")
475	        elif frole is None:
476	            role, why = "excluded", (
477	                "figure_role IS NULL -- ungraded, so nothing states whether this row "
478	                "asserts a value, reports a finding, or states a condition")
479	        else:
480	            role, why = "excluded", (
481	                f"figure_role={frole!r} reports something ABOUT the parameter without "
482	                f"asserting a value for it")
483	            if frole in DIRECTION_SUPPLYING_ROLES and not superseded:
484	                if method in NOT_PUBLISHABLE_METHODS:
485	                    left_out = "skimmed"
486	                    why += (f"; extraction_method={method!r}, so it supplies no direction and "
487	                            f"owes a dedicated reading (owner 2026-10-21)")
488	                elif ctype == "absent":
489	                    left_out = "absent"
490	                    why += ("; claim_type='absent', so it supplies no direction (it can still "
491	                            "confirm through a `confirms` edge)")
492	        out.append({"extraction_id": eid, "ref_id": ref, "figure_role": frole,
493	                    "role": role, "exclusion_reason": why, "superseded": bool(superseded),
494	                    "left_out": left_out})
495	    return out

498	#: NOTATIONS OF ONE QUANTITY, and the arithmetic that relates them. Owner ruling
499	#: 2026-09-17: "Present both -- don't choose between ratio or percentage."
500	#:
501	#: THIS IS A DEFINITION, NOT A CURATED FACT, which is why it is a literal here and
502	#: not derived from the corpus (CLAUDE.md rule 8 asks for derivation of facts the
503	#: machine can compute; the relation between `1:20` and `5 %` is mathematics and
504	#: there is nothing in the database to read it off).
505	#:
506	#: A FAMILY IS NOT A UNIT. Members are two ways of WRITING one dimensionless
507	#: quantity. Millimetres and degrees are different units, and the ruling says so in
508	#: its own ACTION (4): composing across THEM stays refused. Adding a member here is
509	#: a claim that two notations denote the same quantity exactly, which is a
510	#: mathematical claim and should be made deliberately.
511	NOTATION_FAMILIES = {
512	    "gradient": ("%", "rise:run ratio"),
513	}
514	#: Every family member MUST appear here, and the guard below refuses one that does
515	#: not. Without it, adding a notation to the tuple above and forgetting the
516	#: arithmetic makes `to_canonical` fall through to `Fraction(text)` and read the
517	#: number AS IF it were already canonical -- `5` degrees silently becoming `5 %`.
518	#: That is the shape a reviewer of the 2026-09-17 ruling flagged: `degrees` is the
519	#: ARCTANGENT of the ratio, not a rescaling of it, so it is not a notation of this
520	#: quantity at all and belongs to a family of its own or to none. Membership is a
521	#: mathematical claim; this makes forgetting to back it up an error rather than a
522	#: wrong answer.
523	_CONVERTIBLE = {"%", "rise:run ratio"}
524	_RATIO_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*:\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*$")
525	
526	
527	def notation_family(unit):
528	    """Which family a stated unit belongs to, or None if it stands alone."""
529	    for fam, members in NOTATION_FAMILIES.items():
530	        if (unit or "").strip() in members:
531	            return fam
532	    return None
533	
534	
535	def to_canonical(raw, unit):
536	    """One stated value -> an exact Fraction on its family's canonical scale.
537	
538	    The canonical scale is the family's FIRST member -- percent for gradient -- and
539	    the conversion is exact because it is done in Fraction, never float: `1:12` is
540	    100/12, which is 8.333... and is never rounded here. Rounding happens once, at
541	    render, and is marked inexact when it happens.
542	    """
543	    txt = (raw or "").strip()
544	    if not txt:
545	        return None
546	    fam = notation_family(unit)
547	    if fam and (unit or "").strip() not in _CONVERTIBLE:
548	        raise NotImplementedError(
549	            "%r is listed in NOTATION_FAMILIES[%r] but no conversion is defined for "
550	            "it. A family member is a claim that two notations denote ONE quantity "
551	            "exactly; back it with arithmetic in to_canonical/from_canonical, or "
552	            "remove it. Falling through here would read the number as if it were "
553	            "already canonical." % (unit, fam))
554	    m = _RATIO_RE.match(txt)
555	    if m and fam:
556	        rise, run = Fraction(m.group(1)), Fraction(m.group(2))
557	        if run == 0:
558	            return None
559	        return rise / run * 100                      # rise:run -> percent, exactly
560	    try:
561	        return Fraction(txt)
562	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
563	        return None
564

566	def from_canonical(value, notation):
567	    """A canonical Fraction -> (text, exact) in one notation of its family.
568	
569	    `exact` is False when the notation cannot hold the value without rounding --
570	    8.333...% is the case this project actually has -- and the caller MARKS it,
571	    because ACTION (3) of the ruling forbids a rounded figure standing where a
572	    source's own figure would.
573	    """
574	    if value is None:
575	        return None, True
576	    if notation == "%":
577	        as_float = float(value)
578	        text = ("%g" % as_float)
579	        return text, Fraction(text) == value
580	    if notation not in _CONVERTIBLE:
581	        raise NotImplementedError(
582	            "no rendering defined for notation %r; see _CONVERTIBLE" % (notation,))
583	    if notation == "rise:run ratio":
584	        if value == 0:
585	            return "0", True
586	        run = Fraction(100) / value                  # percent -> 1:n, exactly
587	        text = "1:%g" % float(run)
588	        return text, Fraction(1, 1) / Fraction(text.split(":")[1]) * 100 == value
589	    return None, True

592	def bound_on_scale(claimed_value, unit, comparator, claim_type):
593	    """One governing claim -> (lo, hi) as exact Fractions on its family's scale.
594	
595	    The same comparator rules as `parse_bound` -- the comparator IS the bound -- but
596	    the NUMBER goes through `to_canonical`, so `1:20` and `5 %` land on one scale and
597	    can be compared. `parse_bound` is left exactly as it was: it answers "what bound
598	    does this claim state, in its own notation", which is still what the docstring
599	    below promises and what other callers want. This answers the different question
600	    the owner ruling of 2026-09-17 requires, which is "where does this claim sit
601	    relative to one written the other way".
602	    """
603	    raw = (claimed_value or "").strip()
604	    if not raw:
605	        return None
606	    cmp_ = (comparator or "").strip()
607	    if cmp_ == "between" or claim_type == "range":
608	        parts = re.split(r"\s+to\s+", raw)
609	        if len(parts) == 2:
610	            lo, hi = to_canonical(parts[0], unit), to_canonical(parts[1], unit)
611	            if lo is not None and hi is not None:
612	                return (min(lo, hi), max(lo, hi))
613	        return None
614	    v = to_canonical(raw, unit)
615	    if v is None:
616	        return None
617	    if cmp_ in (">=", ">"):
618	        return (v, None)
619	    if cmp_ in ("<=", "<"):
620	        return (None, v)
621	    return (v, v)

1205	    """Cell-scoped derivation sha: identity + governing set + EVIDENCE READ + rule

1207	    checkable).
1208	
1209	    The payload is byte-for-byte what test_db_integrity K01 recomputes when it verifies
1210	    a stored sha, and K01 was re-keyed to (parameter_id × lens) by migration 071. Two
1211	    implementations of one hash that disagree is a hash that attests nothing, so this
1212	    one and K01's move together or not at all. `lens` is the COALESCE value, not the
1213	    whole dict — see lens_key().
1214	
1215	    WHY `n_extractions` IS IN THE PAYLOAD (added 2026-09-10). Without it, two
1216	    materially different cells hash IDENTICALLY, because both have an empty governing
1217	    set:
1218	
1219	        (a) a parameter NEVER READ            — 0 sources, 0 extractions
1220	        (b) a parameter READ AND REJECTED     — 2 sources, 2 extractions, both
1221	                                                non-anchoring on tier (B5a)
1222	
1223	    Reproduced 2026-09-10: both produced f6c0126a5726af3c…. Their gap DESCRIPTIONS
1224	    differ; the attestation did not. B5a creates a new route into that collision class
1225	    and, on today's corpus — where every source's tier is underivable from its own
1226	    (evidence_type, scope) — the universal one. So the sha failed to move across
1227	    exactly the transition this change exists to make visible: somebody reading the
1228	    parameter for the first time.
1229	
1230	    WHY THE COUNT AND NOT THE SORTED GATHERED-REF SET, which is the other candidate
1231	    and carries strictly more information (it would also move when one rejected source
1232	    is swapped for another). K01 must recompute this payload from the database, and
1233	    `specifications` stores neither quantity. A count is recomputable there in one
1234	    line — `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_value_extractions WHERE parameter_id = ?`,
1235	    the whole of `count_extractions()`. The gathered set is not: reproducing it means
1236	    reproducing gather_sources()' DISTINCT and its `superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL`

1238	    from the engine's. A hash whose two implementations can silently disagree attests
1239	    nothing, which is the exact failure this docstring already warns about. The count
1240	    is the largest payload term that keeps one home.

1904	class Refusal(ValueError):

1906

1908	    sentences and leave everything else its traceback. The distinction is load-bearing:
1909	    pydantic's ValidationError IS a ValueError, and a model rejecting a row THIS ENGINE

1911	    (see next_gap_id) would have surfaced had a pending cell ever been replayed. Dressing
1912	    that as a one-line refusal and throwing its location away is how such a defect gets

1916	    `db.py`'s write surface. The duplication is deliberate: this engine's import roster is
1917	    documented per PILOT-MANIFEST.md §4 and reaches only `schemas.*`, and coupling it to
1918	    the write library to share an exception class neither surface ever catches from the

1976	    """This cell must not already carry a determination.

3120	## Owner ruling 2026-09-13 — a code value confirmed by research is upgraded; the empty circle is for code WITHOUT research backing
3121	
3122	> **"Sometimes code standards come from T1. If a code standard is being confirmed as genuine best
3123	> practice according to studies, then the code/regulatory input can be upgraded."**
3124	>
3125	> **"It is when a code/regulatory input does not have research backing that it gets the empty circle."**
3126	
3127	**What this settles.** It was put to the owner as one of three band questions raised by the
3128	2026-09-13 design pass: what strength a cell carries when its *finding* is T1 but its only *value*
3129	comes from a code. The answer is the upgrade route, and it is ruled — not the two-part rendering
3130	that was also on the table.
3131	
3132	**WHAT IT EXTENDS, AND THE EXTENSION IS THE POINT.** `evidence-architecture.md`'s **G1** re-grains a
3133	T4/T5 source out of NON-ANCHORING on exactly one trigger: *"its evidence basis is documented as
3134	traceable to T1/T2 evidence, with that provenance recorded on the source record."* That is a
3135	**genealogy** test — where the number came from. This ruling adds a second, independent route:
3136	**confirmation** — a study finding the code's value sound, whether or not anyone can trace how the
3137	committee reached it. The two are not the same test and the corpus already separates them:
3138	**REF-00980** concludes *"changes to the technical requirements for ramp slope and length cannot be
3139	recommended at this time."* It establishes nothing about ADA's provenance. Under G1 as written it
3140	re-grains nothing. Under this ruling it upgrades the value it confirms.
3141	
3142	**And it makes the empty circle CONDITIONAL where it was automatic.** `tier-system.md` §5 maps T6
3143	(code-floor) to `○` flatly, and §8's band table gives `○ Weak` to "T6 (code-floor)" with a cell whose
3144	entire basis is T4–T6 taking `○` regardless. After this ruling `○` marks the **unbacked** case
3145	specifically: a code or regulatory input with no research behind it. A code value a study has
3146	confirmed is no longer `○` by virtue of being a code.
3147	
3148	**WHAT THE RULING DOES NOT SAY, recorded so nobody fills it in silently.** Three things.
3149	(1) **Which band an upgraded value lands in** — the ruling says "upgraded", not "upgraded to ●". The
3150	natural reading is that it takes the band of the confirming evidence, so a T1 confirmation yields
3151	`●`; that is a reading, not the ruling, and it is the next thing to put to the owner.
3152	(2) **Whether T4/T5 and T6 behave alike here.** The ruling says "code/regulatory input" without
3153	distinguishing them, while existing doctrine splits them — `◐` for T4/T5 citations, `○` for T6.
3154	(3) **What counts as confirmation.** REF-00980's non-recommendation of change is the clear case. A
3155	study that merely *uses* a code value as its rig setting is not confirming it, and that distinction
3156	is exactly what the `confirms` / `tested_at` edges of migration 075 exist to record.
3157	
3158	**Mechanism, so this is executable rather than aspirational.** The 075 design gives the row-level
3159	vocabulary: a `confirms` edge from a finding row to the code figure it confirms is the upgrade
3160	trigger; `tested_at` is not; `insufficient` is the opposite and remains an open band question. The
3161	engine rule that reads those edges is not yet built, so **the upgrade is ruled and unexecuted** —
3162	which is the state an empty table should be read as, per the 2026-09-11 entry above.
3163	
3164	CONDITION: Any session assigning a strength band to a determination whose value comes from a code or
3165	regulatory source, or citing G1's traceability clause as the only re-graining route.
3166	ACTION: Treat confirmation-by-study as a second re-graining route alongside documented traceability.
3167	Read `○` as "no research backing", not as "is a code". Record the confirming relation on the row
3168	rather than asserting the upgrade in prose. Do not assume which band an upgraded value takes — that
3169	is unruled.
3170	DATE: 2026-09-13 — owner ruling, quoted above.

3174	## Owner ruling 2026-09-13 — a derived figure takes a WEIGHTED AVERAGE of its inputs, not the weakest one
3175	
3176	> **"Derived figures are a weighted average of their figures. If something has like two T1 and a
3177	> single T4...it's probably a half circle."**
3178	
3179	**This OVERTURNS the design pass's recommendation**, which was weakest-link: *"a derived figure
3180	anchors at the weakest band of its inputs; if any input is a regulatory-stratum row the derived value
3181	is code-derived (○) regardless."* Under that rule the owner's own example lands `○`. Under this
3182	ruling it lands `◐`. The recommendation is withdrawn; it was session-authored and is not a record
3183	this ruling has to be weighed against (rule 0).
3184	
3185	**It extends a model that already exists.** `tier-system.md` §8, the weighted-strength anchor model
3186	(DR-2026-07-20, owner directive), already holds that *"every tier can anchor a best-practice claim;
3187	the strength of the claim is weighted by the tier of its evidence."* Today's ruling applies that
3188	frame to the composite case — a figure computed from several figures — which §8 never addressed
3189	because derived figures could not be represented at all.
3190	
3191	**THE OPERANDS DO NOT EXIST, and that is the executable gap.** §8 assigns bands by MEMBERSHIP, not
3192	by magnitude: T1/Co-1/T2/Co-2/T3-clinical → `●`; T4/T5 → `◐`; T3-grey/T6 → `○`. There are no numeric
3193	tier weights anywhere in the project. **And the one column whose name promises them does not hold
3194	them:** `weighting_profile.tier_weights` holds audience foregrounding — all five rows are shapes like
3195	`{"foreground":["T1","CO1","conflict_notes","code_refs"],"delta":"show"}`, i.e. which tiers to surface
3196	first for a designer as against a policymaker. A future implementer looking for the weights will find
3197	that column and be misled. Recorded here so they are not.
3198	
3199	**The worked example constrains the function, and the obvious implementation fails it.** Scoring the
3200	bands `●`=3, `◐`=2, `○`=1, two T1 and one T4 average to 2.67, which rounds to `●` — not the half
3201	circle the owner named. **Rounding DOWN yields `◐` and matches.** So the ruling's example is
3202	satisfied by *mean of band ordinals, floored*, and is falsified by *mean, rounded to nearest*. That
3203	is a reading, not the ruling: the owner said "probably", named no weights and no rounding, and the
3204	choice between floor, a tier-count threshold, or genuine per-tier magnitudes is unsettled.
3205	
3206	CONDITION: Any session assigning a band to a `figure_role='derived'` row, or implementing the band
3207	rule in the determination engine.
3208	ACTION: Compute from all inputs; never take the weakest. Do not read
3209	`weighting_profile.tier_weights` as tier weights. Before implementing, put the weighting function
3210	itself to the owner with the 2×T1 + 1×T4 = `◐` case as the acceptance test, and state which candidate
3211	function you propose — do not pick one silently, because more than one satisfies the example and they
3212	diverge on every other combination.

3217	## Owner ruling 2026-09-13 — a finding that a CODE is insufficient supplies no value, and is still first-class evidence
3218	
3219	> **"Insufficient findings don't provide anything, do they? They're insufficient. All you do is log
3220	> you looked at them, I think"**
3221	>
3222	> — put back to the owner because the phrase carries two opposite readings, and confirmed as: **the
3223	> finding supplies no VALUE, but is real evidence.** The cell stays `pending` on value; the finding
3224	> anchors the cell in DIRECTION, remains first-class R7 harm evidence, and is rendered in the book.
3225	
3226	**Why it was queried rather than recorded as first stated.** In the 075 vocabulary `insufficient` is
3227	a RELATION, not a quality grade: it points from a finding row to *the baseline that finding says is
3228	inadequate*. So an "insufficient finding" is a finding **that the code is insufficient** — not a
3229	finding that is itself weak. Read the second way, the ruling would have discarded REF-00784's
3230	*"Between 10% and 100% of users would not be able to maneuver in spaces that meet current
3231	Accessibility Guidelines"* and REF-00971's *"None of the scooters tested were capable of completing
3232	all manoeuvres within the space allowed by existing standards"* as log entries. Those are T1 and T3
3233	findings that the built environment FAILS people, which the research contract's R7 makes first-class
3234	evidence rather than a by-product, and which the mission — *"get people to ask the right
3235	questions"* — points directly at. The clarification preserves them.
3236	
3237	**What the ruling settles.** Such a finding cannot say what the right number IS, so it supplies no
3238	value and cannot move a cell off `pending` on value. It can and does establish that the existing
3239	value is wrong for these people, and that is rendered.
3240	
3241	**The three band questions raised by the 2026-09-13 design pass are now all closed:** a code value
3242	confirmed by research is upgraded and `○` marks unbacked code (entry above); a derived figure takes a
3243	weighted average of its inputs, not the weakest (entry above, weighting function still open); and an
3244	`insufficient` finding supplies direction, not value (this entry).
3245	
3246	CONDITION: Any session grading a finding that a code or standard is inadequate, or implementing the
3247	determination engine's treatment of `insufficient` edges.
3248	ACTION: Never let such a finding supply `value_min`/`value_max`. Never discard it either — it anchors
3249	direction at its own source's tier and is rendered. A cell whose only evidence is `insufficient`
3250	findings is `pending` on value and states the inadequacy.

3255	## Owner ruling 2026-09-13 — grey literature that states a code's value is regulatory stratum, not independent evidence
3256	
3257	> **"If T3-grey is the same value as T6, I think T3-grey is not T3 but T6"**
3258	
3259	**What it is really about, and it is not the marker.** `tier-system.md` §5 maps T3-grey and T6 to the
3260	SAME band — both `○`. So re-tiering such a source changes no marker. What it changes is the
3261	**stratum** it sits in and, decisively, **whether it counts as an independent root**. Two `○` sources
3262	stating the same number read as two sources converging; if one is echoing the other's code, they are
3263	one source counted twice. That is the laundering this project already names
3264	*convergence-not-evidence*, and it is the consequential half of this ruling.
3265	
3266	**Machinery that already exists, so this is not built from nothing.** `v_value_independence` counts
3267	`DISTINCT COALESCE(root_ref_id, root_id)` and admits only `root_type IN ('measurement_primary',
3268	'participatory_finding', 'derived_calculation')` — a row recorded as `committee_assertion` or
3269	`untraced` already corroborates nothing. `echo_of` and `root_id` carry the transmission chain, and
3270	`references/methodology/value-genealogy-worked-example-corridor-width.md` is the worked precedent
3271	(1800 mm's zero in-corpus roots against 2440/2400 mm's two independent roots).
3272	
3273	**THE GAP THIS RULING FILLS.** All of that machinery tests **recorded provenance** — what an extractor
3274	wrote down about where a figure came from. The ruling supplies a test for the case where provenance
3275	was never recorded: **value coincidence with a code**. Grey literature overwhelmingly repeats code
3276	values, and an unrecorded echo currently reads as independent corroboration.
3277	
3278	**THE FALSE POSITIVE, stated because the rule is stated as an identity.** Two genuinely independent
3279	measurements can land on the same number; a code value is often round and grey fieldwork often
3280	reports round numbers. A T3-grey field study that independently measured 1500 mm and a code that says
3281	1500 mm are convergence, not echo, and automatic re-tiering would erase a real corroboration — the
3282	opposite error to the one the ruling prevents, and the harder one to notice afterwards.
3283	**Recommended shape, for the owner to confirm or reject:** the coincidence raises a rebuttable
3284	presumption of echo — the source sits in the regulatory stratum and contributes no independent root
3285	UNLESS its own recorded provenance shows independent measurement (`root_type='measurement_primary'`
3286	with a root that is not the code). That keeps the ruling's force, costs nothing when provenance is
3287	absent, which is the common case, and does not silently delete a genuine second root.
3288	
3289	CONDITION: Any session tiering a grey source whose value matches a code, or counting independent
3290	roots for a parameter.
3291	ACTION: Do not count a grey source as an independent root on value agreement alone. Check its
3292	recorded provenance first; where none exists, treat it as regulatory stratum. Expect no marker change
3293	— both bands are `○` — and expect the change to show up in independence counts and
3294	`regulatory_stratum_only`, which is where it matters.
3295	DATE: 2026-09-13 — owner ruling, quoted above. The rebuttable-presumption shape is a proposal, not
3296	the ruling.

3300	## Owner ruling 2026-09-13 — the derived-figure weighting function: mean of band ordinals, ROUNDED DOWN
3301	
3302	> **"yeah round down"**
3303	
3304	Closing the function left open by the weighted-average ruling above. The band ordinals are the
3305	weights: `●`=3, `◐`=2, `○`=1; the derived figure's band is the **floor** of the mean across its
3306	inputs. Verified against the owner's own worked case and its neighbours:
3307	
3308	| inputs | mean | band |
3309	|---|---|---|
3310	| 2×T1 + 1×T4 — **the owner's example** | 2.667 | **◐** |
3311	| 3×T1 | 3.000 | ● |
3312	| 2×T1 + 1×T6 | 2.333 | ◐ |
3313	| 1×T1 + 2×T6 | 1.667 | ○ |
3314	| 99×T1 + 1×T4 | 2.990 | ◐ |
3315	
3316	**The property that follows from `floor`, recorded so it is a decision and not a surprise.** Only an
3317	all-`●` input set reaches exactly 3.0, so **a single sub-`●` input caps the result below full circle
3318	at any scale** — the last row above. The rule is therefore equivalent to: *a derived figure is fully
3319	anchored only if every input is fully anchored.* That is consistent with the ruling it completes (the
3320	T4 costs you the full circle), and it is the strongest consequence of rounding down rather than to
3321	nearest.
3322	
3323	**What "weighted" means here, stated because it was ambiguous.** The ordinals carry the weighting —
3324	inputs are equally weighted and the tiers differ. If per-input weighting by something else was
3325	intended (sample size, source count, directness), that is a different function and is NOT ruled.
3326	
3327	**Note for the implementer.** `v_best_practice.strength_band` computes a two-value band today; these
3328	are the three `●◐○` bands of `tier-system.md` §5/§8, and no numeric ordinal encoding exists anywhere
3329	in the schema yet. It has to be introduced with the engine rule, not assumed to be present.
3330	
3331	CONDITION: Implementing the band of a `figure_role='derived'` row.
3332	ACTION: floor(mean(ordinal(input bands))), ordinals 3/2/1, inputs equally weighted. Test against the
3333	five rows above; the owner's example is the acceptance case and it falsifies rounding to nearest.
3334	DATE: 2026-09-13 — owner ruling, quoted above.

3590	> the best outcomes is the best range of gradient"**
3591	>
3592	> and, on being shown the limit of that inference:
3593	>
3594	> **"yes it's not perfect it's a proxy"**
3595	
3596	**WHAT THIS SETTLES.** A source that measures the EFFECT of a parameter without prescribing a value
3597	is not silent about that parameter, and judgment may reason from it toward a range. Batch 08 graded
3598	four such sources and the engine returned `pending` with `refs=0`, which reads as "no evidence" over
3599	two studies that measured articular discomfort rising 14→36% and pushrim force more than doubling.
3600	That reading is wrong, and the mechanism is what makes it wrong: `assess_cell.gather_sources()`
3601	gathers `figure_role IN ('claim','derived')` only, so a `finding` contributes nothing to a
3602	determination however much it measured.
3603	
3604	**WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and the limit is the owner's own word — PROXY.** The inference "best
3605	outcomes therefore best range" has a degenerate solution on the evidence as it stands: both curves
3606	are monotonic with no reported plateau, so "best" resolves to 0°, which is not a ramp. A ramp exists
3607	to change level, so the design question is the MAXIMUM ACCEPTABLE gradient, and that needs a
3608	threshold of acceptability which no admitted source supplies. Reasoning from dose-response to a
3609	range is therefore a proxy step and must be marked as one, never recorded as though a source had
3610	stated the value.
3611	
3612	**THE PROJECT ALREADY HAS THE VOCABULARY FOR "PROXY" AND SHOULD USE IT HERE.**
3613	`evidence_population_match.match_grade` carries PROXY for population-of-study vs population-served;
3614	`source_value_extractions.value_directness` exists for how directly evidence bears on the claim and
3615	sits at `NOT_ASSESSED` on every row because no grading rule has been ratified — which
3616	`workplan/2026-09-10-road-to-batch-06.md` makes STOP CONDITION 4, "inventing one is a stop
3617	condition". This statement is NOT read as ratifying a directness scale; it is read as ruling that
3618	the proxy inference is ADMISSIBLE and must be MARKED. The scale itself is still owed.
3619	
3620	**A LEAD THIS OPENS, recorded as a lead and not as a finding.** REF-00985 tested `0° to 4.8°`, and
3621	`arctan(1/12) = 4.76°` — 1:12 being the ramp ceiling in ADA, AS 1428.1, BS 8300-1 and others. If
3622	that ceiling is why 4.8° was chosen, the study measures discomfort across exactly the code-permitted
3623	range and finds it climbing throughout, which under the 2026-09-13 ruling ("a finding that a CODE is
3624	insufficient supplies no value, and is still first-class evidence") makes it a code-insufficiency
3625	finding rather than a bare dose-response curve. THE ABSTRACT DOES NOT SAY THIS. It is an inference
3626	from arithmetic and must be confirmed against the full text before it is filed as anything.
3627	
3628	CONDITION: Any session determining a cell whose evidence measures effects rather than stating values;
3629	any session implementing how `finding` rows reach a determination.
3630	ACTION: (1) A determination may rest on dose-response findings, marked as a proxy, never as a stated
3631	value. (2) `assess_cell` must be able to reach a determination from findings plus a threshold, not
3632	only from `claim` rows — today it cannot, and that is why batch 08 reads `refs=0`. (3) The threshold
3633	half is a code value or an equivalent criterion, and `research_code_leads` names which documents to
3634	fetch but deliberately holds no values (2026-08-12 REFERENCE-ONLY ruling), so it must be retrieved.
3635	(4) Do not invent a `value_directness` scale on the strength of this statement.
3636	DATE: 2026-09-16 — owner statement, quoted above.
3637	
3638	## Owner ruling 2026-09-17 — PRESENT BOTH notations; never choose between ratio and percentage
3639	
3640	> **"Present both--don't choose between ratio or percentage."**
3641	
3642	**WHAT THIS ANSWERS.** The `DEC` gap raised the same day by the ACTION (2) engine work. A gradient is
3643	written as a ratio (`1:12`, `1:20`) by some sources and as a percentage (`5 %`, `6 %`) by others, and
3644	they are the same physical quantity in two notations. `parse_bound` returns `None` for a ratio by
3645	explicit design, so `compose_value` was building the determination's interval out of the
3646	percentage-stated rows alone — measured on parameter 3: **2 of 7 governing claims**, with five rows
3647	dropped. Migration 086 made that visible in `value_note` instead of silent. The question it left open
3648	was whether the engine may convert, and the answer is that the question was malformed: **the engine
3649	does not pick a notation at all. It presents both.**
3650	
3651	**WHAT IT SETTLES.**
3652	
3653	1. **No notation is dropped.** A governing claim stated as a ratio contributes to the determination on
3654	   the same footing as one stated as a percentage. The 2-of-7 composition was a defect, not a policy.
3655	2. **No notation is privileged.** The determination does not select a "canonical" form and relegate the
3656	   other to a note. Both are carried, and a render surface shows both.
3657	3. **Conversion is for COMPARISON, not for replacement.** The engine must compare across notations to
3658	   apply the most-accommodating rule at all, and `1:20 = 5 %` exactly. That comparison is arithmetic.
3659	   What it must not do is overwrite what a source wrote with the other form.
3660	
3661	**WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and the limit is arithmetic rather than doctrine.** Some conversions are
3662	exact and some are not: `1:20` is exactly `5 %`, but `1:12` is `8.333…%` and no finite decimal is the
3663	figure the source stated. So a derived notation is **marked as derived**, and where it does not
3664	terminate it is marked as inexact as well. Presenting both does not license presenting a rounded
3665	figure as though a source had written it — that is the 2026-08-19 shape, one column along.
3666	
3667	**A CONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING.** Until this ruling the engine's protection against inventing figures
3668	was to refuse cross-unit composition outright, which cost it five of seven rows on the first cell it
3669	determined. The protection was real and the cost was invisible. Both halves of that stay true and the
3670	remedy is not to relax the refusal but to stop treating two notations of one quantity as two units.
3671	
3672	CONDITION: Any session composing a determination's value from governing claims stated in more than one
3673	notation of the same quantity; any session extending `parse_bound` or `compose_value`.
3674	ACTION: (1) Compose across notations, never within one. (2) Carry every notation the governing set
3675	states, and mark any notation the engine derived rather than read. (3) Mark a derived notation that
3676	does not terminate as inexact; never round it into the position of a stated figure. (4) This is a
3677	ruling about NOTATION of one quantity, not about UNITS: millimetres and degrees remain different
3678	units and the existing refusal to compose across them is untouched.
3679	DATE: 2026-09-17 — owner ruling, quoted above.
3680	
3681	## Owner ruling 2026-09-18 — UK is canonical; BE, ES, HR, IT and INT admitted to the jurisdiction enum
3682	
3683	> **"UK is canonical, add BE HR INT ES IT to the enum"**
3684	
3685	**WHAT THIS ANSWERS.** `JurisdictionCode` declared 27 codes while the corpus held eight the enum

=== VIEW v_scan_ledger
CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a non-absent extraction exists for the pair (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it.
--   5 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- A reading COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >=
-- parameter_id (the parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that
-- parameter. Rows 1 and 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence
-- than a reading recorded; 3 wins over 4 because a full reading supersedes a partial
-- one of the same source.
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent') THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent') THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.scan_id = b.scan_id

CREATE VIEW v_source_reach_all AS
SELECT
    es.ref_id,
    es.pub_title,
    es.tier                     AS source_tier,
    es.verification_status,
    CASE WHEN ecs.specification_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS reaches,
    ecs.specification_id,
    ecs.parameter_id,
    t.canonical_en              AS parameter_name,
    COALESCE(ecs.identity_code, ecs.icf_code, ecs.needs_code, ecs.medical_code) AS lens_code,
    ecs.state                   AS cell_state,
    (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(ssl.slug, '; ')
       FROM source_slug_links ssl
      WHERE ssl.ref_id = es.ref_id)  AS admitted_under_slugs
FROM evidence_sources es
LEFT JOIN "specification_source_links" csl ON csl.ref_id = es.ref_id
-- THE PREDICATE IS IN THE JOIN, NOT A WHERE. See the header: a WHERE would delete the
-- source from this audit instead of showing that it now reaches nothing.
LEFT JOIN "specifications" ecs ON ecs.specification_id = csl.specification_id
                              AND ecs.retired_at IS NULL
LEFT JOIN base_parameters bp   ON bp.parameter_id = ecs.parameter_id
                              AND bp.status       = 'active'
LEFT JOIN terms t              ON t.term_id       = bp.term_id
-- A TOMBSTONE IS NOT A SOURCE TO REACH WITH. Unlike the specification predicate above,
-- this one belongs in a WHERE: the superseded row is deleted from the audit on purpose,
-- because `by` carries its work (supersede-source).
WHERE es.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL

=== VIEW v_unregistered_roots
CREATE VIEW v_unregistered_roots AS
    SELECT sve.extraction_id,
           sve.slug,
           sve.parameter_id,
           t.canonical_en AS parameter_label,
           sve.root_id,
           'unregistered' AS defect
    FROM source_value_extractions sve
    JOIN base_parameters p ON p.parameter_id = sve.parameter_id
                           AND p.status = 'active'
    JOIN terms t           ON t.term_id      = p.term_id
    WHERE sve.root_id IS NOT NULL
      AND sve.root_ref_id IS NULL
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM external_root_registry err
          WHERE err.root_id = sve.root_id)

    UNION ALL

    SELECT sve.extraction_id,
           sve.slug,
           sve.parameter_id,
           t.canonical_en AS parameter_label,
           sve.root_id,
           'rootless' AS defect
    FROM source_value_extractions sve
    JOIN base_parameters p ON p.parameter_id = sve.parameter_id
                           AND p.status = 'active'
    JOIN terms t           ON t.term_id      = p.term_id
    WHERE sve.root_id IS NULL
      AND sve.root_ref_id IS NULL
      AND sve.root_type IS NOT NULL
      AND sve.root_type NOT IN ('untraced', 'derived_calculation')

=== VIEW v_value_independence
CREATE VIEW v_value_independence AS
    SELECT sve.parameter_id,
           t.canonical_en AS parameter_label,
           COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(sve.root_ref_id, sve.root_id)) AS independent_root_count
    FROM source_value_extractions sve
    JOIN base_parameters p ON p.parameter_id = sve.parameter_id
    JOIN terms t           ON t.term_id      = p.term_id
    WHERE sve.root_type IN ('measurement_primary', 'participatory_finding',
                            'derived_calculation')
      AND (sve.root_ref_id IS NOT NULL
           OR sve.root_id IN (SELECT root_id FROM external_root_registry))
      -- 104: active parameters only; a retired parameter's extractions are history.
      AND p.status = 'active'
    GROUP BY sve.parameter_id, t.canonical_en

25	-- an independent value at all -- exactly the class of error CLAUDE.md section 5(c) warns
26	-- a green gate will not catch, because every field involved is populated and none of
27	-- them is false; the falsity is in what the figure is stated RELATIVE TO, which no column
28	-- anywhere on this table has ever recorded.
29	--
30	-- THE SHAPE OF THE FIX. A comparator is either a ROW this project already holds (another
31	-- extraction, so the two can be joined and reasoned about together) or a LABEL naming
32	-- something the project has not captured as a row (a code clause, a study's own baseline
33	-- sample, a source that names no standard at all). `extraction_relations` records which,
34	-- and the four lens columns on `specifications` (owner 2026-08-28) are the precedent for
35	-- doing this as a typed, checked, real structure rather than a free-text afterthought.
36	--
37	-- WHY ADDITIVE ONLY, NOT A REKEY LIKE 073. Nothing about the evidence->judgment hand-off
38	-- changes -- `source_value_extractions.ref_id` stays NOT NULL into `evidence_sources`,
39	-- and NO UNIQUE index is added anywhere on that table. `scripts/audit/judgment_handoff_shape.py`
40	-- (BLOCKING) polices exactly this shape and this migration gives it nothing to fail on.
41	-- SQLite's ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN accepts a column-level CHECK and a column-level
42	-- REFERENCES; it refuses ADD COLUMN NOT NULL without a DEFAULT once a table holds rows
43	-- (verified against a scratch copy of this table's own row count before writing this
44	-- file), which is why both new columns below are nullable. It also refuses a table-level
45	-- ADD CONSTRAINT outright ("near CONSTRAINT: syntax error", verified the same way), which
46	-- is why every new rule on `extraction_relations` is written into that table's own
47	-- CREATE TABLE rather than bolted on afterward.

49	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
50	-- 1. Two columns on the judgment item. Both start NULL on every existing row; NULL
51	--    means "not yet graded", the same posture `db.py add-extraction` already takes for
52	--    `claim_text` -- required at the CLI, not at the schema, because the schema cannot
53	--    demand a value of eight rows that already exist without one. Grading these two is a
54	--    later writer's job and a later integrity check's job, not this migration's.
55	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
56	
57	-- figure_role -- WHAT KIND OF NUMBER THIS ROW IS, separate from whether it is TRUE.
58	--   claim     -- the source's own headline assertion for this parameter; what most rows
59	--               written before this migration would be graded, once graded.
60	--   finding   -- a result the source reports incidentally while investigating something
61	--               else -- REF-00971's "no scooter completed all five configurations" is a
62	--               finding about existing standards, not a claim about corridor width.
63	--   condition -- a qualifier that only means something attached to another row: a run
64	--               length, a landing rule, a duration, a population subset. Never printed
65	--               alone.
66	--   derived    -- computed from other rows this project holds, never read off the source
67	--               directly. `v_derived_figure_check` below is what re-derives it.
68	ALTER TABLE source_value_extractions ADD COLUMN figure_role TEXT
69	  CHECK (figure_role IS NULL OR figure_role IN ('claim', 'finding', 'condition', 'derived'));
70	
71	-- comparator -- THE ARITHMETIC RELATION BETWEEN THE STORED VALUE AND WHAT IT IS STATED
72	-- AGAINST, when the row has one. A bare number carries none: comparator is NULL, not '='.
73	--   =        -- the source states the value holds exactly, with nothing above or below.
74	--   <        -- the source states an upper bound the value must stay under.
75	--   <=       -- the same bound, stated as inclusive.
76	--   >        -- the source states a lower bound the value must clear.
77	--   >=       -- the same bound, stated as inclusive.
78	--   between  -- the source states a range; claimed_value carries both ends, as the range
79	--             rows on this table already do today (e.g. extraction_id 1's "1:20, 1:16,
80	--             1:12, 1:8").
81	--   approx   -- the source hedges the value itself ("approximately", "around") rather
82	--             than bounding it.
83	ALTER TABLE source_value_extractions ADD COLUMN comparator TEXT
84	  CHECK (comparator IS NULL OR comparator IN ('=', '<', '<=', '>', '>=', 'between', 'approx'));
85	
86	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
87	-- 2. extraction_relations -- the junction that records what a figure is stated relative
88	--    to. One row per comparator edge; an extraction with no comparator gets no row here,
89	--    which is the correct representation of "this figure needed nothing else."
90	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
91	CREATE TABLE extraction_relations (
92	  relation_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
93	
94	  -- THE FIGURE THIS EDGE QUALIFIES. NOT NULL and a real FK -- an edge naming no source
95	  -- row describes nothing. No UNIQUE index touches this column alone: one extraction may
96	  -- carry several comparator edges (a ramp slope is both condition_on a run-length limit
97	  -- AND audited_against a code's stated maximum), and collapsing that to one row per
98	  -- extraction would force a choice this table exists to avoid forcing.
99	  from_extraction_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),
100	
101	  -- WHAT KIND OF COMPARISON THIS EDGE IS. Eight values; the CHECK is the vocabulary
102	  -- (CLAUDE.md section 4) and this is only its meaning, one line each.
103	  --   tested_at        -- the source physically measured its subjects at/against this
104	  --                      referent -- REF-00973's four ramp slopes were each tested_at a
105	  --                      named gradient.
106	  --   audited_against  -- the source measured whether subjects could perform WITHIN a
107	  --                      referent's own stated limit, rather than measuring an
108	  --                      independent value -- REF-00971's "existing standards".
109	  --   confirms         -- an independent measurement agrees with the referent's value.
110	  --   insufficient     -- the source asserts the referent's value is NOT ENOUGH for the
111	  --                      population or task in question -- REF-00784's 10-100% figure.
112	  --   exceeds          -- the source asserts the referent's value is more than needed.
113	  --   delta_over       -- the source states an increment relative to a baseline rather
114	  --                      than an absolute figure -- REF-00976's "more than thirty
115	  --                      centimetres of enlargement over the surveyed stock".
116	  --   condition_on     -- this figure only holds given a second figure this project also
117	  --                      holds as a row -- a slope given its run-length limit.
118	  --   derived_from     -- this figure is computed from the referent, never read off a
119	  --                      source -- always paired with input_role below and always a row
120	  --                      referent, never a label; see the CHECK immediately following.
121	  relation            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (relation IN (
122	                        'tested_at', 'audited_against', 'confirms', 'insufficient',
123	                        'exceeds', 'delta_over', 'condition_on', 'derived_from')),
124	
125	  -- THE REFERENT, HALF A: a row this project already holds. Nullable -- see to_label.
126	  -- Self-joins to the same table this column sits on, which is why the identity CHECK
127	  -- below refuses an edge from a row to itself.
128	  to_extraction_id    INTEGER REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),
129	
130	  -- THE REFERENT, HALF B: prose naming what to_extraction_id would otherwise point at,
131	  -- for a referent this project has not captured as its own row -- a code clause never
132	  -- extracted on its own parameter, a source's private baseline sample, or a referent the
133	  -- source itself never names. Exactly one of this column and to_extraction_id is set on
134	  -- every row; the CHECK enforcing that sits with the rest below, not here, because it
135	  -- names both columns together.
136	  to_label            TEXT,
137	
138	  -- WHAT SORT OF THING to_label NAMES, when it is set. Meaningless and left NULL when
139	  -- the referent is a row instead -- a row already carries this information in its own
140	  -- data.
141	  --   standard      -- a code, guideline or published standard's own stated figure.
142	  --   own_sample    -- the source's own baseline measurement of its own subjects or
143	  --                   stock, as in REF-00976's surveyed housing.
144	  --   prior_source  -- an earlier study or publication, distinct from a code and from the
145	  --                   citing source's own sample.
146	  --   unnamed       -- the source itself does not say what the referent is. See the
147	  --                   `stated` column: this value and 'unnamed' there always travel
148	  --                   together, by CHECK.
149	  to_kind             TEXT CHECK (to_kind IS NULL OR to_kind IN (
150	                        'standard', 'own_sample', 'prior_source', 'unnamed')),
151	
152	  -- HOW EXPLICITLY THE SOURCE ITSELF NAMES THE REFERENT -- independent of whether this
153	  -- project could resolve it to a row. NOT NULL: every edge takes a position on this.
154	  --   named     -- the source identifies the referent by name (a code number, an author,
155	  --              a described sample).
156	  --   unnamed   -- the source gestures at a referent ("existing standards") without
157	  --              naming which one. Never a row referent -- see the CHECK below; naming
158	  --              nothing is not the same claim as naming a specific row.
159	  --   inferred  -- the source names no referent at all and this project supplied one from
160	  --              context (a code the jurisdiction and date make unambiguous). The
161	  --              weakest of the three and the one most likely to need revisiting.
162	  stated              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (stated IN ('named', 'unnamed', 'inferred')),
163	
164	  -- WHICH SIDE OF A DERIVATION this edge supplies. Meaningful only for relation =
165	  -- 'derived_from', enforced by CHECK -- every other relation leaves it NULL.
166	  --   base    -- the starting figure the derived value is computed from.
167	  --   delta   -- the increment added to (or subtracted from) the base.
168	  --   factor  -- a multiplier applied to the base, for a derivation `v_derived_figure_check`
169	  --            does not itself recompute -- that view covers base+delta only; a
170	  --            factor-based derivation is a known residual, not a silent gap, recorded
171	  --            here rather than built speculatively (CLAUDE.md section 8).
172	  input_role          TEXT CHECK (input_role IS NULL OR input_role IN ('base', 'delta', 'factor')),
173	
174	  -- THE SOURCE'S OWN WORDS FOR THE COMPARISON, NOT NULL. Mirrors the verbatim discipline
175	  -- `observed_terms.context_quote` and `db.py add-extraction`'s required `--claim-text`
176	  -- already carry on this project's other judgment-stage rows: a comparator asserted with
177	  -- nothing of the source's own phrasing behind it is not a comparator this project has
178	  -- actually read.
179	  quote               TEXT NOT NULL,
180	
181	  notes               TEXT,
182	
183	  created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
184	  created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
185	
186	  -- An edge cannot compare a figure to itself.
187	  CHECK (to_extraction_id IS NULL OR to_extraction_id <> from_extraction_id),
188	
189	  -- The referent is named as a row or as a label; never as both at once and never as
190	  -- neither, or the edge would point at two things or at nothing.
191	  CHECK ((to_extraction_id IS NULL) <> (to_label IS NULL)),
192	
193	  -- You cannot be conditioned by, or computed from, a figure that does not exist as a
194	  -- row: condition_on and derived_from both require a resolvable to_extraction_id.
195	  CHECK (relation NOT IN ('condition_on', 'derived_from') OR to_extraction_id IS NOT NULL),
196	
197	  -- input_role names which side of a derivation this edge is, so it is meaningless
198	  -- outside relation = 'derived_from' and mandatory inside it.
199	  CHECK (
200	    (relation = 'derived_from' AND input_role IS NOT NULL)
201	    OR (relation <> 'derived_from' AND input_role IS NULL)
202	  ),
203	
204	  -- An unnamed referent cannot simultaneously be one specific known row: if the source
205	  -- does not say what it is, this project cannot have resolved it to a row either.
206	  CHECK (stated <> 'unnamed' OR to_extraction_id IS NULL),
207	
208	  -- Calling the referent's kind 'unnamed' is a claim about how the source stated it, so
209	  -- it must agree with the stated column rather than disagree with it.
210	  CHECK (to_kind IS NULL OR to_kind <> 'unnamed' OR stated = 'unnamed')
211	);
212	
213	-- One edge is one fact; writing the identical edge twice is a duplicate, not a second
214	-- fact, and the COALESCE pair is what lets two NULL-referent rows still collide instead
215	-- of comparing unequal the way raw NULLs would under a plain UNIQUE index.
216	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_xr_identity ON extraction_relations(
217	  from_extraction_id, relation, COALESCE(to_extraction_id, -1), COALESCE(to_label, ''));
218	
219	-- Reader: anything asking "what points AT this figure" -- v_derived_figure_check below,
220	-- and any future audit walking the graph from a referent back to what cites it.
221	CREATE INDEX idx_xr_to ON extraction_relations(to_extraction_id);
222	
223	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
224	-- 3. v_derived_figure_check -- a stored derived value is an ATTESTATION a check
225	--    recomputes, never a number trusted on faith. Same posture as `derivation_sha` and
226	--    K01 (scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py): those re-verify a determination against
227	--    the evidence that produced it; this re-verifies a derived figure against the base
228	--    and delta figures named as its own inputs.
229	--
230	--    ARITHMETIC MODELLED: recomputed = base + delta. That is what input_role names
231	--    'base' and 'delta' mean together, and it covers every derived_from edge pair this
232	--    migration's own examples need. A factor-based derivation (input_role = 'factor')
233	--    is NOT recomputed here -- stated as a known residual above, not silently dropped.
234	--
235	--    "PARSES AS REAL": a GLOB filter, not a full numeric parser -- it accepts a value
236	--    containing only digits, a decimal point, e/E or +/- (and at least one digit), which
237	--    is what CAST(... AS REAL) needs to have parsed something real rather than quietly
238	--    returning 0.0 for text like "1:12" or "12mm". Known residual: a malformed value
239	--    like "3.4.5" passes the filter and CAST silently reads only its "3.4" prefix, the
240	--    same quiet truncation SQLite's own CAST always does. No custom SQL function is
241	--    registered to do better -- this project's readers are plain `sqlite3.connect()`
242	--    calls (CLAUDE.md section 4), and a view that requires a registered function is a
243	--    view most callers cannot open.
244	--
245	--    UNITS: the derived row's own claimed_unit must equal both inputs' claimed_unit
246	--    exactly. No conversion is attempted -- mm compared against inches is a unit-mapping
247	--    problem, not this view's job.
248	--
249	--    Two joins onto extraction_relations, once per input_role, both filtered to
250	--    relation = 'derived_from' and to figure_role = 'derived' on the row being checked
251	--    -- a row that is not graded 'derived' has nothing here to recompute.
252	CREATE VIEW v_derived_figure_check AS
253	SELECT
254	    d.extraction_id                                              AS derived_id,
255	    CAST(d.claimed_value AS REAL)                                 AS stored,
256	    CAST(b.claimed_value AS REAL)                                 AS base_value,
257	    CAST(e.claimed_value AS REAL)                                 AS delta_value,
258	    CAST(b.claimed_value AS REAL) + CAST(e.claimed_value AS REAL) AS recomputed
259	FROM source_value_extractions d
260	JOIN extraction_relations rb
261	  ON rb.from_extraction_id = d.extraction_id
262	 AND rb.relation = 'derived_from'
263	 AND rb.input_role = 'base'
264	JOIN source_value_extractions b ON b.extraction_id = rb.to_extraction_id
265	JOIN extraction_relations rd
266	  ON rd.from_extraction_id = d.extraction_id
267	 AND rd.relation = 'derived_from'
268	 AND rd.input_role = 'delta'
269	JOIN source_value_extractions e ON e.extraction_id = rd.to_extraction_id
270	WHERE d.figure_role = 'derived'
271	  AND d.claimed_value GLOB '*[0-9]*' AND d.claimed_value NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.eE+-]*'
272	  AND b.claimed_value GLOB '*[0-9]*' AND b.claimed_value NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.eE+-]*'
273	  AND e.claimed_value GLOB '*[0-9]*' AND e.claimed_value NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.eE+-]*'
274	  AND d.claimed_unit = b.claimed_unit
275	  AND d.claimed_unit = e.claimed_unit;
276

7758	
7759	    A THIN WRAPPER, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The implementation lived here and walked the
7760	    manifest itself, which put the byte-matching rule in the write path -- a writer that
7761	    verifies itself verifies nothing, which is the reason `retrieval_log.py` is
7762	    deliberately outside that path in the first place (its own module docstring says so).
7763	    It now lives beside the bytes as `retrieval_log.quote_in_artefacts`, where
7764	    `--verify-authors` already lives, and where the normalisation it needs can be reused.
7765	
7766	    THE OLD IMPLEMENTATION WAS A RAW BYTE SUBSTRING and was anti-correlated with
7767	    evidential quality: measured across the ten committed extractions, it rejected two
7768	    genuine quotes -- one because the payload is JATS XML and inline markup splits every
7769	    sentence citing a figure, one because the publisher wrote a space before a full stop

7772	    longer has to survive the publisher's typography.

7774	    return _retrieval_log().quote_in_artefacts(text, ref_id=ref_id)
