## Part A — per question

### Q0. "Stress test pipeline all directions. Attempt to render."

1. **Classification.** GAP (render surface), confidence high; plus one DEFECT in `v_best_practice` (below), confidence medium-high.
2. **Root cause.** RC-H. The walkability output confirms `*<->render NO PATH` in every direction, canonical and populated [V: `walk_populated.txt`]. PLAN step 3.R (Phase 3, render row) is "one renderer over one view to be built", not rehearsed [V]. The view filter `code_floor_only = 0` contradicts ratified doctrine: TIERDOC §8 and ARCH §5 (Option A, owner directive 2026-07-21) say a T4–T6-only cell, T6-only included, renders as weak-band ○ best practice, always flagged; `code_floor_only` is the T6-only subset of `regulatory_stratum_only`, so the view hides exactly the cells Option A says must render flagged [V view SQL; L doctrine]. CONTRACT `specification/no-regulatory-stratum-stated` says such cells "render as weak-band best practice only" [V].
3. **Resolution.** Options: (a) extend `v_best_practice` — rejected, it is a `SELECT *` filter and a renderer needs joins; (b) build 3.R as planned: one view `v_render_cell` (name per 3.R) over live `specifications` (`retired_at IS NULL`, every state including `pending` and `not_applicable`, because METH §2.4 says a pending cell renders `[BEST-PRACTICE-PENDING]` with its gap) joined by pointer to: parameter name (`base_parameters → terms`), lens labels (four registries), the gap (`gaps`), governing sources (`specification_source_links → evidence_sources` with `superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL`), governing and conditioning rows (`specification_extraction_links → source_value_extractions`), the branch view of Q4, the spread view of Q1/E6, the insufficiency view of E4, and `has_unverified_sources`/`marker`/`rests_on_proxy_inference`/`regulatory_stratum_only`/`code_floor_only`/`value_notations`/`value_note`. The renderer owns the register map (ARCH §6 I1–I5) and the weak/code-derived flag text. Recommend (b), and in the same PR retire the `code_floor_only = 0` predicate from `v_best_practice` (or leave the old view unread and name the new one; rule 4 sweep: `v_best_practice` is read by `DB` help text and prose in ARCH §5/§8.3, METH §2.3, CLAUDE §6 — grep before deleting). What wrong thing reaches the book without it: nothing reaches the book at all; and with the current view, a T6-only cell is silently absent rather than flagged.
4. **Where.** render stage, Layer 1 (view) + Layer 2 (renderer). Tooling PR, last of the tooling sequence (it reads everything the other PRs shape).
5. **Verification.** Red today: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_best_practice` = 0 on canonical; on the populated scratch (`stress/populated.db`) a T6-only cell with `code_floor_only=1` is absent from the view. Green: the new view returns one row per live cell of every state; a fixture cell with `code_floor_only=1, regulatory_stratum_only=1, marker='○'` renders with the flag text. Vacuous pass: a view over 0 live rows; avoid by running the renderer's test against `stress/populated.db` (13 cells) and printing `EXAMINED: <rows>`. Probe P-K needs the renderer path added (PLAN 3.R).
6. **Owner rulings.** (R15) "Does a T6-only (code-floor-only) cell render as weak-band best practice, flagged, as Option A says — yes/no?" Default: yes (it is the ratified text). If no, the view's exclusion stands and Option A's text must be amended.
7. **Risks.** The view's stage is the stages of the tables it reads (PLAN 3.R, WALKABILITY finding 1), so the walk into render still shows NO PATH unless the probe maps views or a render-mapped table is read. Rendering before Q4/Q1 land prints "max 5 %" for a stepped rule (the register's own worked render): the renderer must print `value_note` and the branch table or it misleads. Cost: 3.R's 300-line estimate is unverified.

### Q1. Competing rows on one parameter; a gradient of conflicting values across tiers

1. **Classification.** Three items. (a) DEFECT (exclusion-reason text names the wrong cause), high. (b) GAP (no divergence detection; `divergent` never written), high. (c) DESIGN DECISION (tier-blind, most-accommodating selection within the anchoring set; `compose_value`'s own docstring records it as an extension "so it can be vetoed"), high that it is undecided.
2. **Root cause.** RC-D. (a) `ENGINE:gather_extraction_links` lines 469–474: any value-supplying row whose `ref_id` is not in `governing_refs` gets "disqualified on tier, verification or supersession", including a T6 row outranked by anchors (G2) [V]. (b) `determine` never computes agreement; `conv_status` is `pending_assessment` whenever `n_axes >= 2` [V]; the pydantic `ConvergenceAssessment` requires `synthesis_approach` for `divergent` (METH §3.2), which the engine cannot author. (c) `compose_value` lines 920–929 [V].
3. **Resolution.**
   (a) Pass the per-source verdict into `gather_extraction_links` (it already receives `governing_refs`; add a dict `ref -> cause` built in `determine` from `recs`: `disqualified` (`_is_disqualified`), `non_anchoring_on_tier` (`tier_consistent` False), `superseded`, else `outranked_by_stratum`). Text derived from the cause. No schema. Role stays `excluded`; a vocabulary column for the cause would be a second home for a fact derivable from `evidence_sources` at read time — do not add one. The spread (passed-over code floors, ARCH §5 "remain visible as the jurisdiction spread") is then a view over `specification_extraction_links` role `excluded` whose reason starts `outranked` (or, cleaner, over the governing/excluded rows of the regulatory stratum joined on tier), feeding I2's floor-anchor delta. Name what reads it: 3.R.
   (b) Divergence is set logic, not a threshold (rule 7a forbids a hard-coded tolerance): after placing anchoring governing bounds on one scale (`bound_on_scale`), if the intersection of the anchoring sources' intervals is empty (a ceiling below a floor, G8), status = `divergent`. METH §3.3 keeps `stated`; `synthesis_approach` is judgment, so the engine must not invent it: write `divergent` with `synthesis_approach` NULL and cap the cell at `provisional` with a confidence flag naming the divergence (the same cap-and-say-why shape the H4 gate uses, ENGINE lines 1633–1665), until a sanctioned writer records a synthesis approach (a new `DB` verb `record-synthesis-approach --convergence-id --approach --session`, Opus floor per CONTRACT `synthesis/opus-routing`, which then lets re-determination reach `stated`). Within-stratum same-direction disagreement (G3: ≥900 vs ≥1500) is not divergence under floor semantics — the intervals intersect — and most-accommodating is the ruled selection; report the spread in `value_note` (count and range of governing bounds) rather than inventing a conflict.
